Porsche Mission S Gets Visited by the Tuning Fairy – Rendering
11 photos
Photo: Instagram | a.c.g_design
Porsche may be indeed chasing after the money-making segments with all kinds of models that would have seemed impossible for the Zuffenhausen brand until a few years ago, but the company also remains committed to the driver-oriented part of the automotive game with several exciting products.
Here, must obviously name the 911 series, which remains successful, and comprises so many models that one can either deem it a sports car or a supercar, depending on the configuration. The upcoming 718 Boxster and 718 Cayman are also in the making as we speak, and while they were initially supposed to debut as EV models solely, the automaker has changed its mind, after seeing that electric vehicles have started losing ground.
Sticking an ICE unit, probably with some partial electrification, behind the passenger compartment is not enough to do the trick, because Porsche is reportedly not satisfied with how the two cars behave. Thus, it is back to the drawing board, more or less, and that’s why the upcoming 718 series still hasn’t debuted. The latest information suggests that the new Boxster and Cayman might enter production either in 2027 or maybe in 2028.
Now, Porsche hasn’t had an extremely powerful model in its lineup since the 918 Spyder. The spiritual successor to the iconic Carrera GT fought the likes of the Ferrari LaFerrari and McLaren P1, and it saw the light of day between 2013 and 2015 at the Stuttgart factory in Germany. It featured a 4.7-liter V8 assisted by two electric motors for a total of 874 hp (886 ps/652 kW) and 944 lb-ft (1,280 Nm) of torque.
Photo: Instagram | a.c.g_design Back then the 918 Spyder was deemed a hypercar, and it was capable of pushing from 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 kph) in just 2.6 seconds, hitting the 124 and 186 mph (200-300 kph) marks in 7.2 and 19.9 seconds, before topping out at 214 mph (345 kph). Its successor was previewed by the Mission X, an electric study presented more than three years ago (mid-2023), and the production model was initially supposed to go down the EV route.
However, just like in the case of the new 718 series, Porsche changed its mind, and that’s why we now have the Mission S. The latter concept was recently shown to the world, and it sticks to the ICE recipe. For whatever reason, the automaker decided not to detail the oily bits, stating only that it is “a mid-engine sports car platform positioned above the 911 – not as a one-off hypercar, but as a permanent and versatile addition to our customer offering,” as CEO Michael Leiters said.
Porsche’s new Mission S Concept looks like a more advanced 911 at the front, and features an intricate and quite cool (this writer believes) design at the rear, especially with the 917-inspired radiator fan, the flowing rear wing, and the quite uncommon diffuser.
As you already know, this machine has fallen into the hands of the pixel-altering crowd ever since before its grand unveiling. That’s because it was first imagined based on a leaked video, and subsequently, a few wheelmakers wanted a piece of the pie, so they sketched it out on various alloy sets.
Fast-forward to this week, and the Porsche Mission S has been envisioned yet again, this time with an emphasis on the tuning game. It was @a.c.g_design on Instagram who is responsible for the pixel-altering game in this case, which imagines the one-off machine with a more aggressive overall design.
We can see that it has a bigger air intake in the middle of the bumper, a much chunkier splitter, some flaps on the sides of the front bumper, and some add-ons on the front hood. The side skirt attachments have also come from the aftermarket world, and we can see that the back end is home to a new diffuser, and a much larger wing.
Shod in sticky tires from Michelin, the wheels are also part of the CGI makeover. They feature a Y-spoke design, have a brushed silver look, and are pretty much as large as the OEM ones. The Porsche Mission S is now presented in blue instead of white, and it still features quite a few black accents on the outside.
Now, this makeover is definitely on the controversial side of things, in my opinion, anyway, because the car in question looks very aggressive without any outside intervention, not to mention that it is an eye-catching product. But it is still interesting to see what it could look like if it were to go down this route, and to be honest, I’d rather have the regular concept with no mods whatsoever. I also hope that the final production model will stick to this design, because it is a very cool machine.
But do you like the pixel-altered product envisioned here, or would you rather have the regular Porsche Mission S with zero mods? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Λutomotive Custom Garage (@a.c.g_design)
